quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain reduces visibility. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the side of the road and stop until it clears.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Never rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the emergency vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the emergency vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to unload children, you should:

options.text: Wait until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers doing these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: If a transit bus is signaling to return to the main road after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to pull back onto the main road after loading or unloading passengers. Change lanes, slow down, or stop to let the bus safely return to traffic.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch traffic behind you often to see if someone is tailgating or trying to pass. If a car follows too closely, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end accidents happen because cars follow too closely.

questions.question: After a collision, you should:

options.text: Stop at or near the collision. If safe, move your vehicle off the road.
Stand or walk in traffic lanes to wait for help.
Try to remove power lines if they are down in the road.
Move injured people, even if they are not in danger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at or near the collision. If safe, move your vehicle off the road.
questions.explanation: Stop at or near the collision site. If your vehicle can be moved and it is safe, move it off the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols show construction, maintenance, or emergency work ahead.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, what should you do?

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to the one you came from.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to the one you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using emergency lights or sirens. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move out of the way. Drive normally.

questions.question: If your brakes stop working, what should you do first?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times to build pressure.
Flash your lights at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal several times to build pressure.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal several times. This usually builds enough pressure to let you stop.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, especially in crosswalks.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it on a sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle and slash on a sign means that action is forbidden. These signs are white with red and black markings.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your car. A leak lets these gases into the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: What helps prevent crashes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by using signals when slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Look at the entire road and sides ahead.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake.
Look at the center of the road only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and sides ahead.
questions.explanation: Look ahead for problems before you meet them. Scan the entire road, including both sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow backgrounds and black symbols. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: May you drive around or under a gate that is moving up or down at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, as long as a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not hit the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the other vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the other vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give oncoming vehicles at least half of the main travel area. Both drivers need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Assume other drivers will move lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When you are on an entrance or acceleration ramp entering the interstate, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely into traffic when it is clear to do so.

questions.question: When there are no signs or lane markings to control turning, how should you turn?

options.text: Turn from the lane closest to your desired direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn from the lane closest to your desired direction.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to your desired direction and into the lane closest to your current lane.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.
